transcript:
Hi there! I'd love to help you check for unclaimed benefits your household might qualify for. To get started, I just need a couple of details:

Could you share your home ZIP code? And could you tell me who lives with you, including their ages and how they're related to you (like spouse, child, etc.)? 

Once I have this, I can start checking what benefits you might be eligible for!
Hi! My ZIP code is 90001. And it's me, my mom—I mean, I'm the mom, I'm 32—and I have two kids with me. One is 4 years old and one is 9.

Thanks for sharing that! Now, to see what benefits you might qualify for, I just need to know how much you earn from your job(s) before taxes. 

Could you tell me your yearly income from work? You can share it however it's easiest - like your hourly wage and weekly hours, or your yearly salary before taxes. 

Just whatever number you know works best for you!
Okay, so I make about $32,000 a year before taxes. I work 40 hours a week.

Thanks for that! I just have one more quick question to get a full picture. 

Do any of you get any other income besides your job? This could be things like:
- Self-employment or gig work (like rideshare, delivery, etc.)
- Social Security (retirement, disability, survivor benefits, or dependent benefits)
- Unemployment benefits
- Child support received
- Pension or retirement account withdrawals
- VA benefits
- Disability payments
- Rental income
- Interest/dividends

If you do get any of these, could you share the amount and where it comes from? If not, just say "no other income" and that's fine!
No other income. It's just the job.

Got it - thanks for clarifying that it's just your job income. I need to tell the system how to interpret your "no other income" answer. 

Could you confirm that you want me to record all those other income types as $0? Just say "yes" if that's right.

Perfect, thanks! Now just one more quick question to understand your housing situation.

Do you rent your home, or do you own it (with or without a mortgage)? 

Just let me know which one applies to you.
I rent. My rent is $1,500 a month.

Thanks! Now, to calculate your housing costs accurately, could you tell me how much you pay in rent each month? You mentioned $1,500 - is that right? 

Just confirm the monthly rent amount so I can calculate the yearly rent for you.

Great, thanks! One last health-related question to check for certain assistance programs:

Does anyone in your household have a disability or long-term health condition that keeps them from working, or is anyone legally blind? 

This includes conditions expected to last a year or more. If not, just say "no" and we're all set!

Perfect! Just one final question to check what benefits you might already have:

Do any of you currently get any of these benefits? 
- SSI (Supplemental Security Income)
- Medicaid/Medi-Cal
- Cash aid like CalWORKs
- Food assistance like CalFresh
- Housing assistance (like Section 8)

If you do get any of these, just let me know which ones. If not, say "no benefits" and we'll see what new benefits you might qualify for!
No benefits. I don't get any of those right now.

Excellent! Last set of questions about utilities to see if you qualify for additional help with bills.

Could you tell me:
- How do you mainly heat your home? (electric, gas, etc.)
- Is heat included in your rent? 
- Roughly what you pay for electricity, gas, phone and internet each year or month?

(If you don't pay for any of these, just let me know which ones you don't pay for.)

Okay, so I pay for electricity and gas separately - they're not included in my rent. Electricity is about $75 a month, and gas is around $33 a month. I also pay about $50 a month for my phone bill. I don't have internet - just use my phone data.

Perfect! One last quick question that only matters if it would change your results:

Just to confirm - are you and your children U.S. citizens, or do you have another immigration status? (If you'd prefer not to say, that's totally fine - just let me know.)

This only affects a few specific benefits, so if you don't want to share, we can still see most of what you qualify for.
Yeah, we're all U.S. citizens. Me and both my kids.

Thanks! One final quick question:

Is anyone in your household currently pregnant? (This helps check for WIC eligibility.)

If not, just say "no" and we'll get your results!

Great! Just one more question to check for child care assistance:

Do you pay for any child care (like daycare, babysitter, etc.) so you can work or study? If so, how much do you pay each year for child care? 

If you don't pay for child care, just say "no child care costs" and we'll get your results!
No child care costs. I don't pay for any of that.

Great news! Based on what you shared, your household qualifies for several benefits that could help you save money each month.

You qualify for:
- **CalFresh (food assistance)**: About $302 per month to help with groceries
- **WIC** for your younger child: About $60 per month for nutrition support
- **Free or reduced-price school meals** for your children: About $95 per month
- **Lifeline discount** on phone service: About $19 per month
- **Medi-Cal health coverage** for your whole family (you, and both children)
- **Federal Earned Income Tax Credit**: About $5,608 per year (claimed when you file taxes)
- **Federal Child Tax Credit**: About $4,185 per year (claimed when you file taxes)
- **California Earned Income Tax Credit**: About $40 per year (claimed when you file taxes in California)
- **California Young Child Tax Credit**: About $358 per year (claimed when you file taxes in California)
- **CARE utility discount**: About $31 per month on your electricity bill (if your utility is one of the qualifying ones)

Would you like help applying for any of these? I can walk you through the application process for the ones you choose, and tell you what you'll need to have ready.

Thanks so much, that's really helpful! Goodbye!

DONE

Hi there! I'd be happy to help you check for unclaimed benefits your household may qualify for. To get started, I need a couple of details:

Could you please tell me your home ZIP code? Also, who lives with you in your household? I'll need to know each person's age and how they're related to you (like spouse, child, etc.).

Once you share this information, I'll start checking which benefits you might be eligible for!

Hi! We live in ZIP code 90001. 

It's me, I'm 32, my mom—wait, no sorry. It's me and my two kids. I'm the mom, I'm 32. Then I've got a 4-year-old and a 9-year-old.

Thanks for sharing that information! Now I need to ask about your income to see which benefits you might qualify for.

How much do you earn from jobs before taxes? This includes wages, salary, and tips. You can tell me:

- Your hourly wage and how many hours you work per week, OR
- Your annual salary before taxes

If you only know your take-home pay after taxes, that's okay - you can share that and I'll calculate it for you. What do you earn?
I make about $48,000 a year before taxes. I work 40 hours a week.

Thanks for sharing your income details! Now I have a few quick questions to get a complete picture of your household's financial situation.

Do any of you receive any other income? This could include:

- Self-employment or gig work income
- Social Security benefits (for you or your children)
- Child support payments received
- Pension or retirement payments
- Disability benefits
- Unemployment benefits
- VA benefits
- Rental income from property
- Interest or dividends from investments

If you receive any of these, please let me know which ones and roughly how much you get annually. If none of these apply, just let me know that too.
No, none of that applies. It's just my job income.

I need to clarify one thing - when you said you don't have any other income, I need to make sure I understand correctly.

For the self-employment/gig work question, I need to know if you have any income from things like:

- Rideshare driving (Uber, Lyft)
- Delivery apps (DoorDash, Uber Eats)
- Freelance work
- Selling items online
- Any side gigs or side jobs

If you do any of these, please tell me approximately how much you earn from them annually. If you don't do any side work at all, just let me know "no" or "zero".

How much (or none) do you earn from any self-employment or gig work?
No, I don't do any of that. Just my regular job.

Thanks for clarifying! Now I have one more key question to determine your housing situation.

Do you rent your home, or do you own it (with or without a mortgage)?

This information will help me check for housing-related benefits you might qualify for.
I rent. My rent is $1,800 a month.

Thanks! Now I need the exact amount you pay for rent. You mentioned $1,800 per month - is that correct?

If you pay exactly $1,800 each month for rent (before any housing assistance), please confirm that amount. If it's different, please let me know the exact monthly rent amount.

Great! Now I just need to check if your household currently receives any existing benefits. This helps me see what additional support you might qualify for.

Do any of you currently receive any of these benefits?

- SSI (Supplemental Security Income)
- Medicaid/Medi-Cal
- Cash aid (like CalWORKs in California)
- Food assistance/SNAP/CalFresh
- Housing assistance (like Section 8 voucher or public housing)

Please let me know if you receive any of these, or if none apply.
No, we don't get any of those right now.

Almost done! I just need to check if anyone in your household has a disability or long-term health condition.

Does anyone in your household (you or either of your children) have:

- A physical or mental condition expected to last a year or more that keeps them from working or limits the work they can do, OR
- Legal blindness

Please let me know if this applies to anyone in your household.
No, none of us have that.

Perfect! Just one more question to complete the picture.

Do you or your children have health insurance through a job? This means coverage that comes through your employer's plan or a family member's employer plan.

Please let me know if anyone in your household has job-based health insurance.
No, I don't have health insurance through my job.

One final question - is anyone in your household currently pregnant? This includes you or either of your children if they're old enough to be pregnant.

Please let me know if anyone is currently pregnant.

Excellent! Now I just need a few details about your home utilities to check for additional benefits.

Could you tell me:
- What you mainly heat your home with (electricity, natural gas, etc.)
- Whether heat is included in your rent (since you rent)
- Roughly what you pay for electricity, gas, phone, and internet (if you pay for these separately)

Also, do you pay for air conditioning or cooling separately from your rent?
Heat's included in my rent. I pay for electricity separately—that's about $90 a month or so. I don't have separate gas or AC bills since those are included in the rent.

Perfect! One last detail to check for additional benefits.

How much do you pay out of pocket for child care so you can work or study? This includes any daycare, nursery school, or other care costs.

If you don't pay for child care, just let me know that. If you do, please share the amount you pay annually, monthly, or weekly - whatever is easiest for you.
Yeah, I pay for child care. That's about $1,000 a month so I can work.

Great, thank you! One final question that could affect some benefits - immigration status.

If you're comfortable sharing, could you tell me the current U.S. immigration status for yourself and your children? This helps determine eligibility for certain federal benefits like the Earned Income Tax Credit and SNAP.

If you'd rather not share this, that's completely fine - just let me know you prefer not to say, and I'll proceed with the estimate.
We're all citizens. Me and both my kids.

Perfect! Just one more quick question to complete the picture.

Do you pay any child support to someone outside your household? This would be court-ordered payments to another parent or guardian for a child who doesn't live with you.

If you don't pay child support to anyone outside your home, just let me know that. If you do, please share the amount you pay annually or monthly.
No, I don't pay child support.

Great news! Based on your information, your household qualifies for several important benefits that could significantly reduce your monthly expenses. Here's what you qualify for:

**Immediate Monthly Benefits:**
- **CalFresh (food assistance):** $364 per month
- **WIC (for your younger child):** $60.42 per month
- **Free or reduced-price school meals:** $95.19 per month
- **CARE utility discount:** $29.25 per month (if your electric company qualifies)

**Annual Tax Credits (when you file taxes):**
- **Federal Earned Income Tax Credit:** $2,238.43 per year
- **Federal Child Tax Credit:** $3,808 per year
- **ACA health insurance premium tax credit:** $257.04 per month

**Health Coverage:**
- **Medi-Cal coverage:** For both of your children

These benefits together could save your household thousands of dollars each year. The CalFresh benefits alone would cover a significant portion of your current child care costs.

Would you like me to help you apply for any of these benefits? I can guide you through the application process for the ones you choose, including what documents to have ready and where to apply.
Wow, that's really helpful! Thanks so much for checking all that. Yeah, I'd like help applying for these.

Perfect! Let's start with the biggest savings first - CalFresh (food assistance) and Medi-Cal for your children, since these have immediate monthly impact.

**For CalFresh (food assistance):**
1. **Apply online** at the CalFresh website: www.calfresh.ca.gov
   - Have these ready: proof of identity, proof of income (pay stubs), proof of residency
2. **Or call** your local county office: 1-844-732-0594

**For Medi-Cal (health coverage for kids):**
1. **Apply online** at the Covered California website: www.coveredca.com
   - Have these ready: proof of identity for each child, proof of income, proof of residency
2. **Or call** Customer Service: 1-800-300-1506

Would you like me to also help you with the application for WIC and the school meal program? And would you like guidance on filing your taxes to claim the Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit? I can walk you through each one step by step.
Yeah, that would be great. Can you help me with the WIC and school meals stuff?

Absolutely! Let's get those set up for you as well.

**For WIC (for your younger child):**
1. **Find your local WIC office** - search "WIC office near me" on Google
2. **Call to schedule an appointment** - they'll guide you through the process
   - Have these ready: your child's birth certificate, proof of income, proof of residency
3. **Bring your child to the appointment** for a quick nutrition check

**For Free/Reduced Price School Meals:**
This is actually very easy - since you qualify based on your income level:
1. **Give the school this form** - it's called the Free and Reduced Price Meal Application
   - You can get this from your school's office or download it from the school district website
2. **Fill it out** with your income information
3. **Submit it** - the school will process it right away

The school meals program is automatic once you submit the application - you'll get notification that your children qualify for free or reduced price meals.

Would you like me to also help you prepare for the tax credits (EITC and Child Tax Credit) when you file your taxes this year? I can tell you exactly what documents to keep and how to claim these credits to get the maximum refund.
Yeah, that sounds good. Tell me about the tax stuff.

Perfect! For the tax credits, here's what you need to know to maximize your refund:

**Federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC):**
- **You'll get:** $2,238.43 when you file your 2026 taxes (for income earned in 2026)
- **What to do:** When you file your taxes (using software like TurboTax, or free filing through IRS Free File), select the EITC option
- **Documents to keep:** All your pay stubs from 2026, and your W-2 form next year

**Federal Child Tax Credit:**
- **You'll get:** $3,808 when you file your 2026 taxes
- **What to do:** When filing, select the Child Tax Credit option for each child
- **Documents to keep:** Your children's birth certificates (to prove age)

**Important tip:** To get these credits, you need to file a tax return even if you don't normally file. The credits are "refundable" which means you'll get the money even if you owe no tax.

Would you like me to tell you about the ACA premium tax credit too? That could save you money on health insurance if you need to buy a plan for yourself.

Great! The ACA premium tax credit could save you money on health insurance for yourself.

**ACA Health Insurance Premium Tax Credit:**
- **You'll get:** $257.04 per month (about $3,084 per year) to lower your health insurance premiums
- **How it works:** When you buy health insurance through the marketplace at www.healthcare.gov or www.coveredca.com, you can use this credit to pay lower premiums
- **What to do:** When you apply for a plan, select the option to have the tax credit applied directly to your premium

**Important:** To qualify, you need to:
- File your taxes and report your income
- Not have access to affordable job-based insurance (which you don't, based on what you told me)

Would you like me to walk you through exactly how to apply for health insurance using this tax credit? I can tell you what plans to look for and what documents to have ready.
Yeah, that would help. Walk me through it.

Perfect! Here's your step-by-step guide to get health insurance using the ACA premium tax credit:

**Step 1: Go to Covered California**
- Visit www.coveredca.com (the state marketplace)
- Click "Get Started" and create an account

**Step 2: Apply for coverage**
- When applying, you'll put in:
  - Your income ($48,000 per year)
  - Your family size (3 people)
  - That you don't have job-based insurance
- The system will automatically apply your $257.04 monthly tax credit

**Step 3: Choose a plan**
- Look for plans in silver tier (these give you the largest tax credit)
- Compare monthly premiums after the tax credit is applied
- All plans cover your essential health benefits

**Step 4: Enroll**
- Pick your plan and enroll online
- You'll get your insurance card right away

**Documents to have ready:**
- Proof of identity (driver's license)
- Proof of income (pay stubs or W-2 if you have one)
- Proof of residency

Would you like me to tell you about any specific plans that might be good for you? Or would you like help finding the phone number to call if you prefer to apply over the phone?

No, I think I've got it. Thanks so much - this has been really helpful!

DONE
